text:
Rafael Mendes: DR game day #1 (Private) results + fixes before next drill. Thanks everyone who jumped on.

Scenario: lost control-plane Postgres (simulated: DB PVC wiped + pods restarted), restore from last scheduled backup to same cluster (in-place).

Targets we set for the drill:
- RTO: 2h ("standard" tier)
- RPO: 30m

What we achieved:
- RTO: 2h 27m (missed by +27m)
- RPO: 18m (met) (backup age at incident start)

Timeline highlights:
- 00:00 declare scenario start, put cluster in maintenance mode
- 00:11 first restore attempt blocked (object store AccessDenied on list)
- 00:33 permissions workaround applied, reran `rw-private-dr restore execute`
- 01:44 DB restore completed (PITR to T-2m)
- 02:06 control plane up, API reachable
- 02:27 smoke test suite green, maintenance mode off

Evidence doc (notes + commands): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/private-dr-game-day-1
Template we followed: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONCALL/private-restore-drill-template

Biggest sources of time loss:
1) IAM policy mismatch between backup writer role vs restore reader role (we assumed same permissions, not true)
2) Confusion about "maintenance mode" gating vs "stop the world" (we had writes still coming from 2 internal jobs)
3) Restore job timed out once due to default 60m and we didn’t notice until we checked job events

Action items (proposed) — please react / comment if I missed anything. I’ll roll these into ENG-4882 if folks agree.
- [P0] Add explicit preflight check in `rw-private-dr restore plan`: validate object-store perms (List/Get), KMS decrypt, and bucket path existence BEFORE entering maintenance mode.
- [P0] Ship a "break-glass" restore IAM policy snippet in terraform examples (least-priv) + doc when to use.
- [P1] Update runbook to call out the 2 internal writers that must be paused (job names + namespace) and how to verify quiesce.
- [P1] Increase restore Job timeout defaults + surface progress every N minutes in logs so operators know it’s alive.
- [P1] Add dashboard panel: "time since maintenance mode enabled" + annotate restore start/end.
- [P2] Clarify cutover criteria: what constitutes "API reachable" vs "safe to disable maintenance mode" (smoke tests required).

I’m also flagging we need to decide if we want to keep the 2h target for standard tier or adjust to 3h for "first GA" while we harden. My vote is keep 2h and fix the paper cuts.

incident-bot: /restore-checklist → Runbook links: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIVATE/Runbook+Restore+In-Place | Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/private-backup-restore

Sean Gallagher: Nice writeup. :+1: Keeping 2h target IMO. The +27m was basically permissions + lack of preflight. That should be addressable without heroics.

Miles Thornton: +1 keep 2h. Also: we should explicitly track "time to first error". We lost ~20m before realizing the AccessDenied wasn’t transient.

Allison Grant: For observability: we can add a restore phase metric label (plan/preflight/db-restore/artifacts/smoke) so the timeline is obvious from dashboards. Right now we only have job duration and success/fail.

Sergio Costa: Agree. I can take the dashboard changes + alert annotation. If we standardize phase labels now, it’ll help for future drills.

Ethan Park: Re maintenance mode: the control plane API gating worked for external writes, but the internal "policy-sync" job kept retrying and spammed logs. We should treat those as part of the quiesce checklist.

Diego Santos: On the preflight checks: we should run them even earlier, before toggling maintenance mode, but also after (to ensure creds used by restore job match what operator tested locally). We can do both in `restore plan` and `restore execute`.

Connor O'Brien: Re Job timeout: helm charts currently set `activeDeadlineSeconds` = 3600 on the restore job example (copied from generic patterns). That’s too low for PITR + artifact fetch. I’ll patch values + docs.

Talia Benson: I’ll capture these as concrete tasks + owners and link back here. Also can we add a short "RTO math" section in the retro doc? People were counting different start/stop points.

Vivek Kulkarni: From product angle: please keep the tiering message consistent. Standard tier = 2h/30m is what we’ve been saying to pilots. If we need to caveat, I’d rather say "2h with preflight automation enabled" than change the target.

Rafael Mendes: Good call on RTO math. For this drill I used:
- start = scenario declared / decision to restore (00:00)
- stop = smoke tests green + maintenance mode off (02:27)
We can debate if stop should be "API reachable" (02:06) but that would have hidden the last mile risk.

Allison Grant: For alerting: can we add an alert on "restore job failed" that includes the top error line from logs (or at least a link that lands you on logs filtered to that job)? During the drill we bounced between kubectl and grafana.

Sergio Costa: Yep. For now I can add runbook link + logs query link (Loki) with job labels. Extracting top error line is harder but maybe feasible via promtail pipeline later.

Ethan Park: Another thing: DB restore step hit lock contention once when we restarted services in the wrong order (we brought up config service too early). Runbook should specify strict ordering + verification.

Miles Thornton: +1. Ordering should be machine-enforced if possible (restore controller waits for DB ready + migration complete + only then starts dependent deployments).

Diego Santos: We already have some sequencing logic in the installer restore flow but it’s too permissive when a deployment already exists (it assumes "healthy enough"). We can tighten that.

Connor O'Brien: Also: the docs still show `rw-private-dr restore` without the `execute` subcommand in one spot (I saw someone copy/paste the old command). I’ll open a docs PR.

Rafael Mendes: Great. Proposed owners (unless someone objects):
- Preflight perm checks in restore plan/execute: Diego + Ethan
- Break-glass IAM snippet + terraform example: Connor (release) + whoever from infra wants to review
- Quiesce/maintenance mode writer checklist: Ethan + Rafael (SRE)
- Timeouts + helm values: Connor
- Dashboards phase metrics + panels: Allison + Sergio
- Runbook updates + RTO math section: Talia + Kira (Docs)

I’ll file the follow-ups under ENG-4882 and link in here.

Sean Gallagher: Looks good. Please also add an explicit "if preflight fails, do NOT enable maintenance mode" callout in the runbook. We don’t want customers taking themselves down and then discovering permissions are broken.

Rafael Mendes: 100%. Will add.

Talia Benson: Filed: ENG-4882 — "DR game day #1 follow-ups" and linked this thread + evidence doc. Please drop any additional notes in the Linear comments so we don’t lose them.

Vivek Kulkarni: :thumbsup: Thanks all. Let’s schedule drill #2 after we land P0s (ideally before end of month).
